purpose: Doxycycline is an antibiotic used to treat many types of bacterial infections, including chest infections, urinary tract infections, skin infections, and Lyme disease. It is also commonly used to treat acne and to prevent malaria when traveling. Your doctor may prescribe it for other infections as well.
how_it_works: Doxycycline works by stopping bacteria from making the proteins they need to grow and multiply. Think of it like cutting off the bacteria's food supply — without those proteins, the bacteria can't survive. Over time, your immune system can clear out the weakened bacteria and help you feel better.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include nausea, vomiting, stomach upset, and diarrhea. You may also notice increased sensitivity to sunlight, which can make you sunburn more easily. Some people experience heartburn or a sore throat if they don't drink enough water when swallowing the pill.
warnings: Always take doxycycline with a full glass of water and stay upright for at least 30 minutes afterward to avoid irritating your esophagus. Avoid prolonged sun exposure and use sunscreen while taking this medication. Do not take it with dairy products, antacids, or iron supplements close together, as they can reduce how well it works. This medication should NOT be taken by pregnant women or children under 8 years old, as it can affect bone and tooth development.
typical_dosing: The typical adult dose is 100 mg taken twice a day, or sometimes 200 mg once a day, depending on the infection being treated. Always take it at the same times each day and finish the entire course even if you feel better. Take it with food or milk if it upsets your stomach, but avoid dairy within 1-2 hours of taking it.
